title: Choose the app composition
question: Three compositions for the Aether app surface. Lock one.

options.label: The Story
options.thesis: The app reads as a written brief: a lede that says what changed, numbers as punctuation, evidence in chapters below.
options.viewport: Masthead and freshness, a quiet filter strip, the written lede with KPI readings beside it, then the hero chart full width, the next section heading already in view.
options.risk: Only as good as its writing — a weak lede turns it into a slow dashboard, and the answer takes a scroll to reach.

options.label: The Board
options.thesis: Everything visible at once: a KPI row over a disciplined grid of charts and tables, no scrolling on a desktop.
options.viewport: Masthead and freshness, a filter strip, four KPI tiles across, then a two-by-two evidence grid filling the rest of the viewport.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of generic — without strict tile discipline it becomes exactly the dense dashboard it is trying to outgrow.

options.label: The Stage
options.thesis: One fixed composition scaled to the viewport — designed to be read at a distance, in a meeting or an embed.
options.viewport: A title card and one headline reading on the left, a dominant chart on the right, a supporting strip below, controls in a quiet overlay dock.
options.risk: Least suited to daily laptop checking, and the fixed frame wastes space for apps that only hold one or two widgets.
